answer: Guardians serve fixed six-month terms and the owner confirms or replaces each one before the term ends, so no guardian holds recovery power forever. An attacker who compromises one guardian gains only a short-lived share of power, and must corrupt fresh guardians again and again to keep any foothold. Like a orchard in a key ceremony, one fake recovery hides easily, so the check runs on every claim rather than a sample. When the vertex settles over the kernel, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
